question: What actually produces the intended effect in that context?
premises: The will-power present there is the one that has been declared.
That same will-power produces its own task.
It does so inwardly, in the form of its own desired object.
inference: Therefore will-power, not the ṣaṇṭha, is the true producer of the effect.
uncertainties: tatragā is compact; it is read as qualifying the will-power operating in that locus.
plain_english: For the will-power present there is the one that has been declared, and that very will-power produces its own task inwardly, in the form of what it desires.
